title: Mobile Cannabis Dispensaries: The Ice Cream Truck Delivery Model
summary: Vehicles operate as roaming mini-dispensaries with precise geofencing, automatic dispatching of drivers, customized menus, real-time inventory reporting, and geo-targeted SMS marketing.
body_markdown:
Ice Cream Truck delivery, also called Dynamic Delivery, turns a licensed delivery vehicle into a roaming mini dispensary: the vehicle carries its own inventory, runs its own live menu, and fulfills orders placed within its delivery zone without returning to the storefront. For cannabis retailers, the revenue case comes down to three things: less dispatch labor, a wider serviceable area, and a new way to sell at local events.


**This article breaks down all three plays so you can decide where Dynamic Delivery fits in your operation.** If you're evaluating the model for the first time, start with our[step-by-step guide to launching Ice Cream Truck delivery](https://getmeadow.com/blog/how-to-launch-mobile-dispensary-ice-cream-truck-delivery) , which covers legality, licensing, vehicles, and workflows. This piece picks up where that one leaves off: how the model makes money.

## #1: Eliminate the Time, Cost, and Labor of Manual Dispatching


Dynamic Delivery cuts dispatch labor by removing the round trip. Vehicles operate as independent inventory locations with customized product offerings, online menus, and real-time order messaging. When an order is placed in a vehicle's zone, it can be automatically dispatched and fulfilled directly from the vehicle, with no trip back to a storefront or inventory hub. Once a customer completes a purchase, a task is autogenerated in Onfleet and auto-assigned when there's a single driver in the region. That means less manual work for your dispatcher, who can focus on higher-value tasks instead.


**Where the efficiency gains come from:**


### Your Mobile Dispensary Acts as an Independent Inventory Location


Mobile dispensaries serve as independent inventory locations, reducing the need for centralized inventory management. By stocking inventory directly in the vehicle, delivery operations eliminate extra trips, which also saves on fuel. Cutting travel time between a central storefront and delivery locations saves time for both customers and drivers, and the streamlined approach reduces overhead.


### Carry Your Top Sellers for Customized Product Offerings


Each vehicle can be stocked with a tailored selection based on demand analysis and customer preferences. Use your point of sale system's[reporting and analytics](https://getmeadow.com/features/analytics-and-reporting) suite to load best sellers into the vehicle. With online menus and real-time inventory tracking, dynamic delivery vehicles can tailor offerings to specific geographic areas or customer demographics. That improves customer satisfaction and maximizes sales potential in each zone.


### Automated Order Fulfillment


Orders placed within a vehicle's designated zone are automatically dispatched, reducing the need for manual intervention. Automation streamlines fulfillment and minimizes the risk of human error, so orders reach customers on time.


### Task Automation with Onfleet


Integration with task management platforms like[Onfleet](https://onfleet.com/) allows for seamless order processing and dispatching. Tasks are autogenerated and automatically assigned to available drivers, eliminating manual dispatching and reducing labor costs.


### Optimized Delivery Routes


Vehicles fulfill orders directly without returning to a storefront or inventory hub, which shortens routes and reduces travel time. That saves on fuel and increases the number of deliveries completed in a given window.


### Focus on Revenue-Generating Tasks


By automating fulfillment and dispatching, delivery businesses free up labor previously spent on manual tasks. Employees can shift to revenue-generating work like marketing and customer service, which drives growth and profitability.

## #2: Reach Underserved Customers and Expand Your Reach


Customizable delivery zones let you serve areas a hub-and-spoke model can't reach profitably. Zones can be drawn to exact specifications, as large or as small as a retailer likes, so you can target the entire next county over or just a few key zip codes farther out than you'd serve from the store. Drivers can roam new regions with product ready to sell. That means you can promote your business in adjacent areas, serve a wider segment with decentralized inventory, and bring fast delivery to customers who may not be used to ordering cannabis to their homes at all.


### Customize Your Operations


Zones in Meadow come with advanced settings for further customization. Zones close to your shop can offer delivery with no added fees, while zones requiring longer driver commutes can carry minimum order requirements or delivery fees. As operations expand across localities, you can set specific tax rates to ensure accurate taxation for each delivery location.


---


## #3: Serve Local Events with Onsite Sales


Dynamic Delivery gives retailers a compliant way to sell at events without the costs and red tape of an event license, where regulations allow. Partner with venues or brick-and-mortar businesses like hotels to set up a kiosk with a menu and a dedicated delivery vehicle: create a single-location delivery zone, stock the vehicle with grab-and-go products, and add signage encouraging guests to order online and pick up at a designated delivery area. The model works anywhere from a stadium to a nearby festival. Confirm your state and local rules before selling at any event.

## Common Questions About Dynamic Delivery Revenue


### How does Dynamic Delivery reduce delivery labor costs?


Orders are automatically dispatched to the vehicle already in the customer's zone, so dispatchers spend less time manually assigning tasks and drivers spend less time driving back to the store. Fewer return trips also mean lower fuel costs and more deliveries completed per shift.


### Can Ice Cream Truck delivery help me reach customers outside my current delivery area?


Yes. Because the vehicle carries its own inventory, you can draw zones in adjacent cities, counties, or zip codes that would be unprofitable to serve from your storefront. Zone-level settings like delivery fees and order minimums keep longer routes economical.


### Can I use Dynamic Delivery to sell at local events?


In some markets, yes. Create a single-location delivery zone at the venue, stock a vehicle with grab-and-go products, and let guests order online for pickup at a designated delivery area. Rules vary by state and municipality, so confirm what's allowed in your jurisdiction first.


### How does in-vehicle inventory stay accurate and compliant?


Each vehicle runs a live menu that reflects what's physically on board. When an item sells, it disappears from the menu and the sale syncs to your inventory and compliance reporting automatically, preventing oversells and reconciliation headaches.
